global_issues.title: Treasury doubles debt buybacks, yields drop sharply
global_issues.note: Confirmed by CNBC, Bloomberg, WaPo (2026-08-19). Treasury doubled long-bond (10-30yr) buyback size to at least $4B/operation. Note the upsized operations are forward-dated (effective Sept 9-Nov 4), though the yield reaction was same-day: 30y -9bp to 5.196%, 10y -5.7bp to 4.647%. The briefing's 'immediately' correctly describes the yield move but could mislead on when actual buying starts. Buybacks followed a selloff that pushed 30y yields to their highest since 2007, amid Iran/Israel war escalation fears and total US debt topping $40T.

global_issues.title: Oil near 3-week high on Hormuz and Iran tensions
global_issues.note: Substance is directionally correct: Hormuz shipping disruption and US-Iran tensions remain elevated with tanker transits down sharply. However, the '$91' figure is wrong for WTI -- WTI closed around $85-86 on 2026-08-19; $91 is the Brent crude price, not WTI. The briefing appears to have conflated the two benchmarks. The '3-week high' framing is also unverified in search results.

missing_major_news.title: Cybersecurity sector de-rating: CRWD -5.3%, PANW -5% despite analyst price-target hikes
missing_major_news.impact: CRWD and PANW dropped on valuation/profit-taking ahead of CrowdStrike's Aug 26 earnings (trading >166x forward P/E), even as Mizuho, Truist, and Cantor Fitzgerald raised price targets ($240-$250). This is a sector-specific de-rating story, not general 'momentum slowdown' as the briefing's sector analysis implies.

missing_major_news.title: Tesla Cybercab Austin wireless-charging hub permit filing
missing_major_news.impact: Named as the specific catalyst (via news reports) for TSLA's +4.23% surge on 2026-08-19, alongside the broader yield-driven rally. The briefing attributes TSLA's move only to macro conditions/DOWNTREND-vs-price divergence without mentioning this company-specific catalyst.

missing_major_news.impact: Broader fiscal backdrop to the Treasury buyback story; not stock-specific but relevant context for the rates/yields narrative supporting NVDA, MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL.

sector_check.note: The laggards line miscategorizes CRWD, a pure-play cybersecurity name, as a 'semiconductor equipment and software' name lagging on 'momentum slowdown.' The actual driver was a cybersecurity-sector de-rating (CRWD -5.3%, PANW -5%) tied to elevated valuations ahead of CRWD's Aug 26 earnings -- notably occurring despite three sell-side price-target increases, meaning it reflects position-trimming/valuation reset rather than negative momentum or slowing fundamentals.

grok_report.summary: The core macro narrative (Treasury buybacks lowering yields) is well-sourced and accurate, and individual watchlist prices/percentages (NVDA, CRWD, TSLA) check out against independent data. However, the oil benchmark is misstated (Brent's $91 print reported as WTI, which was actually ~$85-86), the sector analysis mischaracterizes CRWD's cybersecurity-specific de-rating as generic momentum slowdown, and the 'green'/91.1 mood score overstates a market that only posted a modest +0.21% gain against a backdrop of near-2007-high long yields and active Hormuz supply risk.
